edits.find:
Two questions, in order. First, which nephritis: hematuria with protein, hypertension, edema and a rising creatinine two weeks after a sore throat is poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis. A latent period of weeks, not days, separates it from IgA nephropathy; no rash and a normal blood count set aside IgA vasculitis and HUS.

Second, what the kidney needs. Inflamed glomeruli filter less, so the kidney retains salt and water, and the edema and hypertension both come from that volume. The first drug is a loop diuretic, with sodium and fluid restriction; saline, tempting for the oliguria, would worsen the overload. The disease is self-limited, so plasmapheresis has no role, and an ACE inhibitor is used with caution because it can raise potassium in AKI; if pressure stays high after diuresis, add a calcium channel blocker.
edits.with:
The combination of hematuria with protein, hypertension, edema and a rising creatinine two weeks after a sore throat is poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis. A latent period of weeks, not days, separates it from IgA nephropathy. No rash and a normal blood count set aside IgA vasculitis and HUS (hemolytic uremic syndrome).

Inflamed glomeruli filter less, so the kidney retains salt and water. The edema and hypertension both come from that volume. The first drug is a loop diuretic, with sodium and fluid restriction. Saline for the oliguria would worsen the overload. The disease is self-limited, so plasmapheresis has no role. Use an ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor with caution, because it can raise potassium in AKI (acute kidney injury). If pressure stays high after diuresis, add a calcium channel blocker.
